                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Migrating from the Wasp TS Config\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Function: job() - Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-13, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/api/@wasp.sh/spec/functions/job)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'> **job**(`fn`, `config`): `Job`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Creates a Job definition.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Pass the worker\n'[39m +
                      [32m'function as the first argument and configure the executor and schedule\n'[39m +
                      [32m'in `config`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`Reference`<`AnyFunction`>\n'[39m +
                      [32m"The async function that performs the job's work.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'It receives the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'submitted args and a context containing the declared entities.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Required `executor` and optional `schedule`, `entities`,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'and `performExecutorOptions`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### executor ​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`"PgBoss"`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Executor backing this job.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Currently only `"PgBoss"` is available.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### performExecutorOptions?\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`ExecutorOptions`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Executor-specific default options used when submitting the job.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'These options are passed through to the executor and can be overridden\n'[39m +
                      [32m'when submitting the job or by Schedule.executorOptions for scheduled runs.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`Schedule`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Cron schedule that runs the job automatically.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"import { job } from '@wasp.sh/spec'\n"[39m +
                      [32m"import { foo } from './src/jobs/bar' with { type: 'ref' }\n"[39m +
                      [32m'job(foo, {\n'[39m +

                      [32m"entities: ['Task'],\n"[39m +
                      [32m"schedule: { cron: '0 * * * *' },\n"[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Recurring Jobs | Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-05, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.11.8/advanced/jobs)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Start by creating a Job declaration in your\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'job mySpecialJob {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'executor: PgBoss,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'perform: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'fn: import { foo } from "@server/workers/bar.js"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'entities: [Task],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'executor: PgBoss,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'job mySpecialJob {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'executor: PgBoss,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'perform: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'fn: import { foo } from "@server/workers/bar.js",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'executorOptions: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pgBoss: {=json { "retryLimit": 1 } json=}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'schedule: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'cron: "*/5 * * * *",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'args: {=json { "foo": "bar" } json=},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'executorOptions: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pgBoss: {=json { "retryLimit": 0 } json=}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'entities: [Task],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The Job declaration has the following fields:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'-\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'required\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m' ```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"import { PG_BOSS_EXECUTOR_NAME } from '@wasp/jobs/core/pgBoss/pgBossJob.js'"[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# https://wasp.sh/llms-full.txt\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-09, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/llms-full.txt)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'##### Jobs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'| Name                  | Type           | Notes                                                                                                                                        |\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'| `PG_BOSS_NEW_OPTIONS` | Stringoptional | A [JSON env var](#json-env-vars).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Enables you to provide [custom config](https://wasp.sh/docs/advanced/jobs#pg_boss_new_options) for PgBoss.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Start by creating a Job spec in your Wasp file:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="main.wasp.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app, job } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { mySpecialJob } from "./src/workers/bar" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'spec: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'job(mySpecialJob, {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'executor: "PgBoss",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'entities: ["Task"],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The worker function must be an `async` function.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"The function's return value represents the Job's result.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The following casing conventions have now become mandatory:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Operation (i.e., Query and Action) names must begin with a lowercase letter: `query getTasks {...}`, `action createTask {...}`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Job names must begin with a lowercase letter: `job sendReport {...}`.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# How to Run CRON Jobs in Postgres Without Extra ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-05-28, last updated: 2026-07-21, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/blog/2025/05/28/how-to-run-cron-jobs-in-postgress-without-extra-infrastructure)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Declarative job definitions** – define jobs directly in your Wasp config.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Everything just works** – no need to manually set up workers or queues.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'action scheduleEmailSummary {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'fn: import { scheduleSummaryEmail } from "@src/matches/operations",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'entities: [Match]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'job sendEmailSummaryJob {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'executor: PgBoss,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'perform: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'fn: import { sendEmailSummary } from "@src/workers/schedule",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'entities: [Match]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"As you can see above, the `sendAt` variable determines the job's execution time.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'Just provide a date to the `delay()` function, and the job will execute at that specified time.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Setting up a recurring job is even simpler than a scheduled job, because we don't need an `action` to execute it.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'We can simply define the interval in the `job` declaration.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Whether you're queuing up daily digests, reminders, or any time-based workflow, the setup is refreshingly simple:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'- Define a `job` in your Wasp config.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Use `.delay()` for specific future times.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Use `cron` for recurring schedules.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# vibe-coding-video/.cursor/rules/6-advanced-troubleshooting.mdc at video-starter · wasp-lang/vibe-coding-video\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-04-11, last updated: 2025-06-08, [Read more](https://github.com/wasp-lang/vibe-coding-video/blob/video-starter/.cursor/rules/6-advanced-troubleshooting.mdc)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Wasp supports background jobs, useful for tasks like sending emails, processing data, or scheduled operations.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Jobs require a job executor like PgBoss (which requires PostgreSQL, see [3-database-operations.mdc](mdc:.cursor/rules/3-database-operations.mdc) ).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Example Job definition in [main.wasp](mdc:main.wasp):\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'job emailSender {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'executor: PgBoss, // Requires PostgreSQL\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Define the function that performs the job\n'[39m +
                      [32m'perform: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'fn: import { sendEmail } from "@src/server/jobs/emailSender.js"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Grant access to necessary entities\n'[39m +
                      [32m'entities: [User, EmailQueue]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Jobs can be scheduled or triggered programmatically from Wasp actions or other jobs.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Build Your Own Personal Twitter Agent 🧠🐦⛓ with LangChain\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2025-11-04, [Read more](https://wasp-lang.hashnode.dev/build-your-own-personal-twitter-agent-with-langchain)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`{=psl psl=}` syntax in the entities above.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This denotes that anything in between these\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`psl` brackets is actually a different language, in this case, Prisma Schema Language.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To do so, let’s go to our\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`main.wasp` file and add our job at the very bottom:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'job newIdeasJob {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'executor: PgBoss,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'perform: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'fn: import generateNewIdeasWorker from "@server/worker/generateNewIdeasWorker.js"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'entities: [User, GeneratedIdea, Tweet, TweetDraft],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'schedule: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// run cron job every 30 minutes\n'[39m +
                      [32m'cron: "*/30 * * * *",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'executorOptions: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pgBoss: {=json { "retryLimit": 2 } json=},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'with\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`perform`we’re telling the job what function we want it to call:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`generateNewIdeasWorker`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'just like actions and queries, we have to tell the job which entities we want to give it access to.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In this case, we will need access to all of our entities.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We also tell pg-boss to retry a failed job two times.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# How to handle scheduled jobs in a load-balanced Wasp ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-09-27, last updated: 2026-03-25, [Read more](https://www.answeroverflow.com/m/1421515585069645895)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Current job definition: job dailyStatsJob { executor: PgBoss, perform: { fn: import { calculateDailyStats } from "@src/analytics/stats.js" }, schedule: { cron: "0 1 * * *" } } Any guidance would be greatly appreciated!\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**No, you do not need to designate a primary instance.** All instances can safely run PgBoss, and the coordination is handled at the database level.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Regular jobs: when you invoke them in Wasp, they get inserted in the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pgboss.job\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'table and then one of the workers will pick them up\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Scheduled jobs: PgBoss itself keeps checking the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pgboss.schedule\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'table if some job needs to be invoked, and when the time comes, PgBoss inserts the job in the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pgboss.job\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'| pgboss.schedule |<------->| Application (schedule MyJob) |\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'| (SQL poll: is it time to run MyJob?)\n'[39m +
                      [32m' v\n'[39m +
                      [32m'+------------------+\n'[39m +
                      [32m'| pgboss.job | <--- new row inserted for MyJob at scheduled time\n'[39m +
                      [32m'+------------------+\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"| (Worker polls for state='created')\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# wasp-jobs - Skill - Smithery\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-12-01, last updated: 2026-04-14, [Read more](https://smithery.ai/skills/ToonVos/wasp-jobs)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Requires PostgreSQL database.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Complete Job Setup Workflow\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 1.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Define Job in main.wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'job emailSender {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'executor: PgBoss, // Requires PostgreSQL\n'[39m +
                      [32m'perform: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'fn: import { sendEmail } from "@src/jobs/emailSender.js"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'entities: [User, EmailQueue] // Entities needed in job\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Job options:**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'job myJob {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'executor: PgBoss,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'perform: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'fn: import { myJobFunction } from "@src/jobs/myJob.js"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'entities: [User, Task],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'schedule: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'cron: "0 0 * * *", // Daily at midnight\n'[39m +
                      [32m'args: {=json { "foo": "bar" } json=} // Optional default args\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 2.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Implement Job Function\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Quick Setup Checklist\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Switch to PostgreSQL (if using SQLite)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Define job in main.wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Implement job function\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Restart `../scripts/safe-start.sh` (multi-worktree safe)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Test job submission\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Add error handling\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Set up monitoring/logging'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Scheduling email sending with Pg-boss - Wasp - Answer Overflow\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-06-21, last updated: 2026-03-25, [Read more](https://www.answeroverflow.com/m/1253704995442790512)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Here's how you can set up a job with\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. **Declare the Job**: In your\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'main.wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'file, declare a job that uses\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'pg-boss\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'perform\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'field should import the function that will be executed when the job runs.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This function should be responsible for filtering tasks and sending the email digest.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'schedule\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'field should contain the cron string for scheduling the job.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'args\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'field can be used to pass arguments to the function.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'entities\n'[39m +

                      [32m'import { myMiddlewareConfigFn, mySetupFunction } from "./src/myServerSetupCode" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'server: {\n'[39m +

                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### setupFn?\n'[39m +
                      [32m'​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'> `optional` **setupFn?**: `Reference`<`AnyFunction`>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Async function called once on server start.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Wasp awaits it before the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'server accepts requests.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Receives a context containing the Express `app`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'and underlying `http.Server`, so you can register custom routes, set up\n'[39m +
                      [32m'additional databases or WebSockets, or kick off scheduled jobs.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In TypeScript, you can type the function with the `ServerSetupFn` type\n'[39m +
                      [32m'from `wasp/server`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### Example ​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { type ServerSetupFn } from "wasp/server"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const mySetupFunction: ServerSetupFn = async () => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'await setUpSomeResource()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# https://wasp.sh/llms-full.txt\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-09, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/llms-full.txt)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`setupFn` declares a Typescript function that Wasp executes on the client before everything else.\n'[39m +
                      [32m':::caution[The setup function can also run on the server]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The setup function can also run during server-side rendering, like when [prerendering](https://wasp.sh/docs/advanced/prerendering) pages, where browser APIs like `window` are not available.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Project Setup / Server Config\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can configure the behavior of the server via the `server` field of `app` spec:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="main.wasp.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app } from "@wasp.sh/spec"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { myMiddlewareConfigFn, mySetupFunction } from "./src/myServerSetupCode" with { type: "ref" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default app({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name: "MyApp",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'server: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'setupFn: mySetupFunction,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'middlewareConfigFn: myMiddlewareConfigFn,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Setup Function\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`setupFn` declares a Typescript function that will be executed on server start.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```ts title="main.wasp.ts"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { app } from "@wasp.sh/spec"'[39m
                  },

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Build a metrics dashboard with background jobs in Wasp\n'[39m +

                      [32m'### server.setupFn for queue setup ​\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Thankfully, Waspleau can leverage a powerful and flexible hook supplied by Wasp called `server.setupFn`.\n'[39m +

Wasp\'s built-in background job executor, **PgBoss**, only works on PostgreSQL, so once the migration is done you must also add a PgBoss background job to justify (and exercise) the new database. This entity must be created by your new PostgreSQL migration.             [32m'When using the newTask tool, the agentType parameter is optional. Leave it empty (None) to launch a generic sub agent, or specify one of the available agent types below to select a specialized agent.\n'[39m +
            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +
            [32m'Web browser automation agent for navigating websites, interacting with pages, and extracting information. Uses agent-browser CLI for browser control, including headless sessions and optional local Chrome auto-connect.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of questions this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "where is the authentication logic implemented"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "find all usages of the config parser"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how does the ignore-walk module work"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### guide\n'[39m +
            [32m"A comprehensive guide for learning about Pochi's capabilities, features, and configuration.\n"[39m +
            [32m'This agent helps users understand how to use Pochi effectively, fetch documentation, and modify their config file (.pochi/config.jsonc) with proper confirmation.\n'[39m +
            [32m"**IMPORTANT: Any request to modify Pochi's configuration must be handled by this agent.**\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Trigger examples:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- General info: "what can Pochi do?", "what agents/tools are available?", "how does Pochi work?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### planner\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to formulate comprehensive, technical implementation strategies for feature development, system refactoring, or defect resolution.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to planning and architectural design; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a plan to implement the user authentication feature"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how should we refactor the database schema"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "design a solution for the memory leak issue"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +

            [32m'- "check this code and leave feedback"\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Always include a reminder in your prompt to ensure the result will be submitted through the `attemptCompletion` tool.\n'[39m +
            [32m'If the task stops without submitting the result, it will return an error message.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Usage notes:\n'[39m +

            [32m'3. Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report.
